projects.title: TripBuddy
projects.description: Adaptive travel companion that re-plans your trip when plans break.
bullets: Led a team of four from a 24-hour NewHacks build to a product a startup acquired two weeks after the live demo, with a full codebase handover in June 2026.
Took it on a real trip and watched four first-time users fail at flows I was sure were intuitive. That proved the problem was comprehension, not performance, and justified a full rebuild.
Built a linked-list itinerary engine that reshuffles flexible stops around locked flights and hotels, with Gemini checking opening hours, weather and travel time, plus Expedia PDF import.

projects.title: DealFlow OS
projects.description: Startup intelligence platform for investment firms, built and run solo.
bullets: Built and still operate the platform solo. It runs in production at three professional services firms, and I defined the usage and scoring metrics it reports on.

My first version let an LLM write research memos and nobody could verify the output, so I rebuilt it: memos assemble deterministically from source records and the model only polishes wording. A rate limit degrades phrasing, never a figure.
Analysed behavioural usage data to separate momentum signals from noise, then shipped dashboards on top across 500+ production deployments, fed by scheduled scraping and enrichment pipelines.

projects.title: swamr
projects.description: One prompt spins up 150+ specialist Cursor agents that build your project in parallel.
bullets: Built and published a framework that coordinates 150+ specialist agents across planning, build, test and hardening phases, running up to 20 Cursor agents at once.
Designed mandatory human review gates so generated work stays a draft until a person validates it, plus checkpointing that resumes an interrupted run exactly where it stopped.
Gave every agent a shared Obsidian memory and wired MCP servers to GitHub, Supabase and Slack, so agent #150 knows what agent #1 decided.

projects.title: Vedocker
projects.description: Docker and Kubernetes rebuilt from scratch in Go. Paste a GitHub URL, get a running container.
bullets: Wrote a container runtime, image store, build engine, networking and orchestration from the ground up on Linux namespaces, cgroups and iptables. No Docker Engine, containerd or Kubernetes underneath.
Swap github.com for the dashboard URL and it clones, builds and runs the repo. If there is no Dockerfile, Gemini writes one. Also ships as an MCP server and a browser extension.
Published a technical write-up, "I built my own Docker and Kubernetes system from scratch", on Towards AWS.

projects.title: Revenant
projects.description: AI memory for engineering teams. Ask anything about how your team works.
bullets: Won the sponsor prize for best use of memory architecture at GenAI Genesis 2026.
Co-built a system that embeds GitHub, Slack and Jira activity into a pgvector index and answers natural-language questions over it, so knowledge stays when people leave.
Designed the schema and query paths to split a low-latency retrieval path from a batch evaluation path, so batch processing stopped blocking live requests.

projects.title: stockbot
projects.description: A rules engine finds the trade. A local LLM gets veto power.
bullets: Built an intraday trading bot where deterministic Python finds and sizes setups, and an LLM judge can only say no. It can't create a trade, change config or override a risk gate.
Made the judge fail-closed: a timeout, an error or an off-format answer means veto. Every yes and every no is logged with its reason.
Added nightly post-mortems that turn losing patterns into AVOID rules the judge enforces the next day. Paper trading by default, with backtests and safety tests.

projects.title: CineSync
projects.description: Scheduling and disruption intelligence for film productions.
bullets: Turns a script and call sheet into a dependency graph of scenes, actors, locations and shoot days, then runs Monte Carlo simulation to score schedule volatility.
Eight background agents (weather, budget drift, schedule drift, actor, location and more) flag risk continuously, with a live reasoning console so crews can see why.
Git-style schedule branches: drag scenes between days on a storyboard and see budget deltas and conflicts before merging. Locked down with RBAC, rate limiting and row-level security.

projects.title: Surfacer
projects.description: Drop in your LinkedIn export, get a ranked list of exactly who to message.
bullets: Scores every connection into seven configurable tiers with a 0 to 100 score, the reasons behind it and a ready-to-send opener.
One deterministic scoring engine shared by a Next.js web app, a CLI and a Manifest V3 Chrome extension.
Private by design: no backend, no API keys, no AI calls. The CSV never leaves your machine, and spreadsheet-formula injection is neutralised on export.

projects.title: Finger Musix
projects.description: Play piano, guitar, flute and drums by pinching your fingers on camera.
bullets: On-device MediaPipe hand tracking in the browser, with a One Euro filter per landmark and pinch detection that fires a camera frame early.
Synthesised every instrument in code so a pinch schedules sound in under 1 ms. Guitar strings, drum skins and piano keys are real mass-spring physics.
Adaptive quality keeps it smooth on weak devices, and the camera feed never leaves the device.

projects.title: Model Evaluation & Benchmarking
projects.description: Protein-language-model pathogenicity detection, built in 36 hours.
bullets: Comparisons at a 36-hour research hackathon were being made on whichever run looked best, so I built an evaluation harness that scored every configuration on identical metrics.
Ran parallel AWS SageMaker training jobs on ESM2 protein language models and ClinVar data to fit the experiment loop inside the deadline.
Separately, evaluated frontier models for a founder and wrote the recommendation selecting Llama 3.1 8B on licensing and architecture grounds, in language she could act on.

projects.title: AI Ticket-to-PR Automation
projects.description: From a Jira ticket to an open pull request, automatically.
bullets: Built an MVP that creates Jira tasks with AI, cuts a GitHub branch per ticket, generates the change and opens the pull request.
The repository is the demo: every branch and PR in it was produced by the pipeline itself.
Became the foundation for an internal implementation at Savi Finance, extended on AWS.

projects.title: CallBooker
projects.description: A phone number that answers, books and follows up like a front desk.
bullets: Turns a Twilio number into an AI receptionist for restaurants and small businesses: it takes the call, books the slot and confirms the details.
Gemini extracts structured booking intent, ElevenLabs speaks, and Cal.com checks availability and creates the booking.
Follows up by SMS and email asking for a review, with credentials kept out of code.

projects.title: UniSolved
projects.description: One plain-language question in, a concrete next step out, for U of T students.
bullets: Combines a direct answer, ranked campus resources and mentor matches in one chat workflow.
Ranks mentors on course overlap, language, program fit and topic relevance, and puts official campus support first when a question calls for it.
Gemini with Google Search grounding when a key is present, with a full local fallback when it isn't.

projects.title: Pawgress
projects.description: Voice-first to-do app where getting things done keeps your puppy happy.
bullets: Say a task out loud and it gets tracked, reminded and ticked off automatically. Built for people with ADHD.
SwiftUI app on a Django JWT API, with Deepgram speech-to-text and transcripts stored for review.
Ties productivity to caring for a virtual pet, so the reward loop feels emotional rather than administrative.

projects.title: Helping Hand
projects.description: A voice and vision controlled bionic arm.
bullets: Say "pick up the red ball" and the arm finds the object, approaches it and grasps it.
Combined speech recognition with object detection, then chose between a full grip and a two-finger pinch from the object's size and shape.
Integrated servo motors and microcontrollers, and tuned for real-time sync between voice and vision.

projects.title: PromptBoards
projects.description: Organise, share and reuse AI prompts like tools instead of chat history.
bullets: Boards by topic or workflow, search across boards and prompts, and filters by category and model.
React frontend on Vercel and a Django API on Render, with auth and environment configuration done end to end.
The first project I took all the way from localhost to production.

projects.title: SecureNotes
projects.description: Encrypted notes with a Rust WebAssembly frontend.
bullets: Rust and Yew frontend compiled to WebAssembly, on a Django REST backend.
JWT issuance and validation, protected routes and per-user data ownership modelled at the database level.
Postgres on Supabase, so notes follow the user across devices without giving up access control.

projects.title: Local-First Password Manager
projects.description: A Chrome extension that keeps your vault on your device, not a company's cloud.
bullets: Detects password fields and surfaces the vault at the right moment, unlocked by a master password.
Credentials are encrypted and stored locally. No central backend to breach.
Built to reduce how much users have to trust third parties with their most sensitive data.

projects.title: mARry-me
projects.description: AR wedding planning, built in 37 minutes at Cursor Toronto.
bullets: Ideated and built in 37 minutes at a Cursor Toronto hackathon.
A BERT classifier pulls each partner's interests from their Claude chat history, and Gemini turns them into prompts for a real-time AR scene with under 3 s latency.
Voice commands change the scene, add supplies to an Amazon cart through Playwright and email nearby vendors through Resend.

projects.title: Smart Air
projects.description: Android asthma companion for kids, parents and doctors.
bullets: Built the one-tap triage flow, personal-best peak-flow zones and the action-plan authoring screen.
Wired parent alerts when rescue-inhaler use crosses a safety threshold in a three-hour window.
Parent-controlled sharing means providers see nothing until a parent opts in.

projects.title: Self-Updating Portfolio
projects.description: This site. An n8n workflow keeps it in sync with my GitHub.
bullets: An n8n workflow watches GitHub for new repositories on a schedule.
It reads each README, extracts the project details and categorises them with custom logic.
It writes the result into the projects.json this page renders from, so shipping a repo updates the site.
